title: Persistent Unhealthy systemd Service State
exclusions: Detects two consecutive non-healthy observations for explicitly inventoried system-level systemd `.service` units on Linux hosts running the custom collector. It does not discover which services ought to run, monitor user service managers, prove application-level reachability, measure response time, identify root cause, detect a collector that has stopped sending, or establish regulatory compliance. A unit intentionally inactive under socket, timer, path, or dependency activation must not be placed in the always-active inventory.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `linux_systemd_service_not_active` saved-search definition, its scheduler and alert history, the versioned `services.list` assigned to each host class, and dashboard exports containing `host`, `service_name`, `status`, `sub_state`, `load_state`, `systemctl_rc`, `latest_observed_epoch`, and `health_reason`. These artifacts show configured monitoring and observed results; they are not runtime-validation or compliance evidence by themselves.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At dispatch time 2026-07-28T09:20:00Z, index two events for `host=service-test-positive service_name=uc-test.service` at observed epochs 1785230280 and 1785230340 with `event_version=1 load_state=loaded status=failed sub_state=failed systemctl_rc=1 collection_status=ok`. Run the SPL with matching fixed time bounds and its freshness comparison anchored to that dispatch time. Expect exactly one row with `samples=2`, `unhealthy_samples=2`, `status=failed`, and `health_reason=active_state_failed`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: For `host=service-test-negative service_name=uc-test.service`, index an event at epoch 1785230280 with `status=failed sub_state=failed systemctl_rc=1`, followed at epoch 1785230340 by `status=active sub_state=running systemctl_rc=0`; set `event_version=1 load_state=loaded collection_status=ok` on both. The same bounded search must return zero rows because only one of the two most recent observations is unhealthy.

dataSources: A locally managed Splunk Universal Forwarder scripted input runs on each systemd host every 60 seconds and writes one event per inventoried unit to the deployment-selected `index=os`, `source=linux_service_status`, and local-convention `sourcetype=linux:service_status`. The custom event contract requires `event_version`, `observed_epoch`, `service_name`, `load_state`, `status` (systemd `ActiveState`), `sub_state`, `systemctl_rc`, and `collection_status`; `host` and `_time` are Splunk metadata.
app: Splunk Universal Forwarder native scripted input packaged in the locally managed `linux_service_status_input` app. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux is not required and does not define this custom sourcetype or event contract.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:service_status" earliest=-4m@m latest=@m
| fields _time host event_version observed_epoch service_name load_state status sub_state systemctl_rc collection_status
| eval observed_epoch=tonumber(observed_epoch), systemctl_rc=tonumber(systemctl_rc)
| where event_version="1" AND isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(service_name) AND isnotnull(observed_epoch)
| sort 0 host service_name -observed_epoch -_time
| dedup host service_name observed_epoch
| streamstats count as sample_rank by host service_name
| where sample_rank<=2
| eval unhealthy=if(collection_status!="ok" OR load_state!="loaded" OR status!="active" OR systemctl_rc!=0,1,0)
| eval health_reason=case(collection_status!="ok","collection_error",load_state!="loaded","load_state_".load_state,status!="active","active_state_".status,systemctl_rc!=0,"is_active_nonzero",true(),"healthy")
| eval latest_status=if(sample_rank=1,status,null()), latest_sub_state=if(sample_rank=1,sub_state,null()), latest_load_state=if(sample_rank=1,load_state,null()), latest_systemctl_rc=if(sample_rank=1,systemctl_rc,null()), latest_collection_status=if(sample_rank=1,collection_status,null()), latest_health_reason=if(sample_rank=1,health_reason,null())
| stats count as samples sum(unhealthy) as unhealthy_samples max(observed_epoch) as latest_observed_epoch values(latest_status) as status values(latest_sub_state) as sub_state values(latest_load_state) as load_state values(latest_systemctl_rc) as systemctl_rc values(latest_collection_status) as collection_status values(latest_health_reason) as health_reason by host service_name
| where samples=2 AND unhealthy_samples=2 AND latest_observed_epoch>=now()-180
| eval observation_age_seconds=now()-latest_observed_epoch
| table host service_name status sub_state load_state systemctl_rc collection_status health_reason samples unhealthy_samples latest_observed_epoch observation_age_seconds
| sort 0 host service_name
description: Reports one row per Linux host and inventoried systemd service when its two most recent 60-second observations are both unhealthy. An observation is unhealthy when collection failed, the unit definition is not loaded, systemd `ActiveState` is not `active`, or `systemctl is-active` returns nonzero; the newest observation must be no more than 180 seconds old.
value: Detecting a persistent unhealthy service helps operators restore an essential daemon after a crash, failed deployment, dependency problem, or accidental stop before the outage spreads. Requiring two observations reduces alerts from brief restart transitions while preserving the exact systemd state needed for triage.
implementation: Deploy the exact `linux_service_status_input` app to systemd-based Linux Universal Forwarders, maintain an approved `.service` allowlist for each host class, and run its scripted input every 60 seconds into the locally selected operating-system index. Verify the versioned key-value contract and compare each unit with `systemctl show` and `systemctl is-active`; then schedule the search every minute and alert only after two consecutive unhealthy observations.
visualization: Use a current-fault table showing `host`, `service_name`, `status`, `sub_state`, `load_state`, `health_reason`, and observation age. Add a fleet matrix of host by service using the latest state and a separate collection-freshness panel; do not color a host green merely because no service-status event arrived.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned package or application deployment restart** — `dnf`, `yum`, `apt`, RPM/DEB maintainer scripts, or a release tool can keep a service non-active across two polls. Match the exact host, unit, and minute to an approved change before suppressing the alert; confirm the next observation is active.

2. **Intentional stop during maintenance** — Database backup, filesystem repair, certificate replacement, or cluster failover procedures can deliberately stop a named unit. Require a bounded maintenance record for that host and unit and preserve the observed state in alert history.

3. **Activation-managed unit in the wrong inventory** — A socket-, path-, timer-, or on-demand-activated service can correctly be `inactive` while idle. Check `systemctl show` relationships and the unit's operating design; remove it from the always-active `services.list` rather than suppressing every inactive result.

4. **Oneshot service without `RemainAfterExit=yes`** — A successful oneshot unit normally returns to inactive after its action. It is unsuitable for this availability rule unless its unit semantics intentionally remain active; monitor its result or timer separately.

5. **Host-role reassignment or package removal** — A stale inventory entry yields `load_state=not-found` or another non-loaded state after the service is intentionally removed. Reconcile the host class and approve an inventory revision; do not hide all not-found units globally.

**Suppression mechanism:** if local policy requires suppression, use an owner-approved, time-bound exception register keyed by exact `host` and `service_name`, with UTC start/end epochs, reason, and change ID. Apply only currently active entries, prohibit wildcards and non-expiring entries, and retain the base unsuppressed result for review.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational systemd service availability monitoring; no adversary behavior asserted)
reviewer: Cursor AI documentation-only review against systemd and Splunk primary sources; no runtime validation or SME sign-off
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and state semantics

Deploy a Splunk Universal Forwarder on each systemd-based Linux host and manage a private deployment app named `linux_service_status_input`. This is a local app name, not a Splunkbase product. The forwarder service account must be able to execute `/usr/bin/systemctl` and query the system service manager; test that access as the forwarder account before rollout. Do not add sudo if ordinary read-only systemd introspection works. Grant the Linux operations role search access to the selected event index and permission to create the saved search, but not broad Splunk administration rights. The catalogue uses `index=os`; this is an explicit deployment choice, so change the input and SPL together if another approved index is used.

Build an owner-approved inventory for each host class. Include only system-level names ending in `.service` that are expected to remain active. Record package ownership, service owner, dependency, and maintenance policy outside the event payload. Do not include oneshot services that normally return to inactive, or units designed for socket, path, timer, or on-demand activation. Unit names are queried one at a time: systemd documents that `systemctl is-active` succeeds if at least one of multiple supplied units is active, so batching units into one command would conceal individual failures.

The custom `linux:service_status` contract is version 1 and emits one whitespace-delimited key-value event per inventoried unit: `event_version=1 observed_epoch=INTEGER service_name=UNIT.service load_state=VALUE status=VALUE sub_state=VALUE systemctl_rc=INTEGER collection_status=ok|error`. `status` is exactly systemd's high-level `ActiveState`; it is not a CIM field. `load_state` is `LoadState`, and `sub_state` is systemd's unit-type-specific `SubState`. The collector uses `systemctl show` because systemd designates it for computer-parsable property output, and it runs `systemctl is-active --quiet` separately. Treat return code zero only as active and every nonzero value as non-active or command failure; do not assign undocumented meanings to individual nonzero codes.

## 1. Package the exact collector and input

Create `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_service_status_input/bin/service_status.sh`, owned by the forwarder account and executable with mode `0755`, with this complete POSIX shell body:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -u
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
LC_ALL=C
export PATH LC_ALL
: "${SPLUNK_HOME:?SPLUNK_HOME is required}"
services_file="$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_service_status_input/local/services.list"
if [ ! -r "$services_file" ]; then
    printf 'services list is not readable: %s\n' "$services_file" >&2
    exit 1
fi
observed_epoch=$(date +%s)
while IFS= read -r unit || [ -n "$unit" ]; do
    case "$unit" in
        ''|'#'*) continue ;;
        *[!A-Za-z0-9_.@:-]*)
            printf 'invalid service unit in services.list: %s\n' "$unit" >&2
            continue
            ;;
        *.service) ;;
        *)
            printf 'unit does not end in .service: %s\n' "$unit" >&2
            continue
            ;;
    esac
    properties=$(systemctl show --no-pager --property=LoadState --property=ActiveState --property=SubState "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
    show_rc=$?
    load_state=$(printf '%s\n' "$properties" | awk -F= '$1 == "LoadState" {print substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1); exit}')
    active_state=$(printf '%s\n' "$properties" | awk -F= '$1 == "ActiveState" {print substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1); exit}')
    sub_state=$(printf '%s\n' "$properties" | awk -F= '$1 == "SubState" {print substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1); exit}')
    systemctl is-active --quiet "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1
    active_rc=$?
    collection_status=ok
    if [ "$show_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$load_state" ] || [ -z "$active_state" ] || [ -z "$sub_state" ]; then
        collection_status=error
        [ -n "$load_state" ] || load_state=unknown
        [ -n "$active_state" ] || active_state=unknown
        [ -n "$sub_state" ] || sub_state=unknown
    fi
    printf 'event_version=1 observed_epoch=%s service_name=%s load_state=%s status=%s sub_state=%s systemctl_rc=%s collection_status=%s\n' \
        "$observed_epoch" "$unit" "$load_state" "$active_state" "$sub_state" "$active_rc" "$collection_status"
done < "$services_file"
```

Create `local/services.list` with one approved unit name per line. Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored; the script rejects whitespace, shell metacharacters, and entries not ending in `.service`. Keep different host-role inventories in separate deployment-app assignments rather than shipping a fleet-wide superset. The script emits one event even for a known unit that is inactive, failed, masked, or not found. If the list itself is unreadable it exits nonzero and writes only an error to the forwarder's internal log, which is why collector freshness must be monitored separately.

Enable the collector in `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_service_status_input/local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_service_status_input/bin/service_status.sh]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
source = linux_service_status
sourcetype = linux:service_status
```

Splunk documents that a numeric scripted-input interval is measured in seconds and that the next interval follows completion. At `N` inventoried units, this design produces `1,440 × N` small events per host per day; measure script duration and ingest volume before broad deployment. The script must complete comfortably within 60 seconds. Do not use `interval=0`, which means continuous restart, and do not edit files under a product `default` directory.

Configure the source type in the app's `local/props.conf` on the parsing and search tiers required by the deployment topology:

```ini
[linux:service_status]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
TIME_PREFIX = observed_epoch=
TIME_FORMAT = %s
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 12
KV_MODE = auto
AUTO_KV_JSON = false
```

`TIME_*` settings make `_time` the observation epoch at parse time; `KV_MODE=auto` extracts the versioned `key=value` fields at search time. Ensure the relevant settings are present on each tier that performs those functions. The forwarder uses its configured `host` metadata; the script does not invent an asset identity. No HEC token, external API, inbound listener, Splunk premium app, or Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux input is part of this design.

## 2. Verify collection and the event contract

Run the script as the forwarder service account on one representative host. Expect exactly one line per valid inventory entry and no stdout other than contract events. For each unit, compare the event with `systemctl show --property=LoadState --property=ActiveState --property=SubState UNIT.service` and run `systemctl is-active --quiet UNIT.service; printf '%s\n' "$?"` immediately afterward. A changing unit can legitimately transition between the commands; repeat the check when values disagree.

Inspect the merged configuration with `$SPLUNK_HOME/bin/splunk btool inputs list --debug` and verify that the enabled stanza, 60-second interval, index, source, and sourcetype come from the intended local app. Search `index=os sourcetype="linux:service_status" earliest=-10m | table _time host event_version observed_epoch service_name load_state status sub_state systemctl_rc collection_status`. Confirm all required fields exist, `event_version` is `1`, epoch values are numeric, each host/unit normally has one event per minute, and the newest event agrees with the same host's systemctl output. Reject mixed contract versions, duplicate stanzas, shared `host` identities, or values containing whitespace before enabling an alert.

## 3. Save, understand, and tune the search

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_systemd_service_not_active` and schedule it with cron `* * * * *`. Its explicit `earliest=-4m@m latest=@m` window examines four closed minute buckets. Sorting newest first, discarding duplicate copies of the same `host,service_name,observed_epoch` observation, and assigning `sample_rank` retains exactly the two newest distinct observations for each host and service. The row survives only if both are unhealthy and the newest `observed_epoch` is no more than 180 seconds old. With a healthy 60-second input, two consecutive polls represent approximately 60 seconds between observations. This persistence threshold is a catalogue starting point, not a systemd or Splunk default.

An observation is healthy only when `collection_status=ok`, `load_state=loaded`, `status=active`, and `systemctl_rc=0`. The output uses the newest event for displayed state and derives a specific `health_reason`. Trigger the alert when result count is greater than zero, notify once per `host,service_name`, and deduplicate repeated actions for five minutes while preserving every scheduled result in alert history. For an especially restart-sensitive service, require three samples only after changing the lookback and documenting the longer detection delay. For a service whose approved restart routinely exceeds one minute, use a bounded maintenance exception rather than weakening every unit's threshold.

The primary search intentionally does not equate missing events with healthy service. Add a separate freshness search that compares the latest `observed_epoch` per expected host with inventory and alerts when it is older than 180 seconds. A host never seen by Splunk requires an external expected-host list; it cannot appear from absence alone. There is no valid CIM accelerated equivalent for these locally defined fields, so do not manufacture a `tstats` search over a CIM data model.

## 4. Validate logic without claiming production execution

Perform the positive and negative scenarios in this record in a test index with the same field extraction. Use fixed search bounds around the stated epochs and replace the dynamic `now()` freshness comparison with the stated dispatch epoch for repeatability. The two failed positive observations must produce one row with two unhealthy samples. The failed-then-active negative sequence must produce no row. Add three further checks: two active samples must return no row; `collection_status=error` on both samples must return one `collection_error` row; and a newest observation older than 180 seconds must return no service-state row but must be caught by the separate freshness control.

On an authorized lab host, stop a disposable service that is explicitly approved for testing, wait for two polls, and compare the result with `systemctl show` and `journalctl --unit` output. Restart it and confirm the alert clears after the next healthy sample enters the two-sample window. Record the search job ID, raw events, unit journal, and restoration evidence when that runtime test is actually performed. This editorial review assessed documentation and logic only; it did not execute the script, index fixture events, stop a service, or validate a Splunk version.

## 5. Dashboard, response, evidence, and troubleshooting

Build a current-fault table and a host-by-service latest-state matrix, but place collector freshness beside them. Link each fault to raw events and the host runbook. On alert, first verify `observed_epoch`, host identity, inventory assignment, and current `systemctl show` values. Then inspect `systemctl status UNIT.service` for human-readable context and `journalctl --unit UNIT.service` for the failure interval. Check dependencies, package or release changes, configuration validation, resource exhaustion, and restart policy before taking action. Restore service only through the owning team's procedure; this monitoring search must not automatically restart units or reboot hosts.

Retain the saved-search definition, app and inventory revision, alert history, dashboard export, and authorized test records under the organization's operations-evidence policy. These artifacts establish what was configured and observed, not application reachability, root cause, service-level-objective attainment, or regulatory assurance.

No events commonly means the app was not assigned, the stanza is disabled, the script or list is not readable, `systemctl` is outside the restricted path, the forwarder cannot query the system manager, forwarding is blocked, or the input routes to another index. Inspect `_internal` records for the scripted input and `ExecProcessor`, then run the script as the forwarder account. Raw events with null fields indicate the `props.conf` search-time configuration is absent or the sourcetype spelling differs. Duplicate events indicate duplicate input stanzas or overlapping app assignments. Repeated `load_state_not-found` results usually indicate a stale package/unit inventory. A permanently inactive oneshot or activation-managed unit indicates the wrong monitoring contract, not a service outage. Use only exact-host, exact-unit, expiring maintenance exceptions, and keep the unsuppressed base results available for review.
grandmaExplanation: We check that each essential background service on a Linux server stays running, and we wait for two checks before raising the alarm. That helps the team catch a real stop without overreacting to a momentary restart.
